Subject: Tool calling patterns & auth — follow-up + next steps

Hi Elena / FinTech Team,

Thanks again for the productive discovery call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock down scope for the POC workshop: 

Recap (high level)
- Goal: Replace the current ad-hoc retrieval + enrichment pipeline with a resilient tool-calling architecture that supports low-latency client chat and overnight batch reranking.
- Constraints: Data must stay in your VPC for PHI-like fields, keys managed via your KMS, and any retrieval calls should respect tenant isolation.

Redwood recommendations (short list)
1) SDK & auth
   - Use Redwood server-side SDK in your backend for user-originated flows.
   - Auth: OAuth2 short-lived tokens for user-scoped actions; server-to-server calls use mTLS or API keys rotated through your KMS.
2) Routing & policies
   - Latency-priority route for interactive chat (pin to regional low-latency pool).
   - Cost-priority route for batch embedding/rerank jobs (use deduped batching, quantized model variant).
3) Structured output & tool definitions
   - Define tool contracts as small JSON schemas (name, inputs, outputs, timeout_ms, retry_policy).
   - Recommend determinism for tools used in business-logic (DB lookup, account lookup) and allow non-deterministic LLM calls downstream for summarization.
4) Parallel tools pattern (proposed)
   - Fan-out independent deterministic tools (retriever, enrichment API, external risk check) in parallel.
   - Merge responses into a single context vector, then run a reranker (embeddings + logistic scorer) to pick top candidates.
   - For interactive calls, return first-pass answers from the fastest deterministic tools while reranker completes asynchronously.
5) Error handling
   - Timeouts for each tool (e.g., 300ms for lookup, 2s for enrichment).
   - Circuit breaker: on repeated failures fall back to a cached answer or degrade to safe default.

Proposed immediate next steps
- Technical workshop (90 min): deep-dive on SDK setup, auth, routing policies, and walk the tool definition format.
- Deliverable after workshop: light SOW + implementation checklist (we attached a draft SOW).

Availability: I can run the workshop Wed 9/16 or Fri 9/18 morning PT. Please confirm preferred time and any internal participants.

Attachments: FTT-POC-SOW-draft.pdf, sample tool-defs and schema examples (attached).

Thanks — looking forward to the POC.

Best,

Elena — perfect, thanks for confirming. Answering your asks and adding a few implementation notes so your SRE can pre-check: 

Security checklist (short)
- SOC2: We will provide our SOC2 Type II report and map controls relevant to access logging and key management.
- Audit logs: Redwood can emit per-request audit events to your destination (S3/CloudWatch) with tokenized identifiers.
- KMS: server API keys can be stored and rotated using your KMS; for highest assurance we recommend mutual TLS for server-to-server calls.

Tool-definition sample (high level)
- name: account_lookup
- inputs: {account_id: string, tenant_id: string}
- outputs: {balance: number, status: string, last_updated: timestamp}
- timeout_ms: 300
- retry_policy: {retries: 1, backoff_ms: 200}

Parallel tool pattern (details)
- Fan-out: retriever + risk_check + enrichment in parallel.
- Merge: normalized JSON into a single context object; if any deterministic tool returns a 'hard block' flag, surface immediately and halt LLM actions.
- Rerank: embeddings + lightweight classifier to pick top N results for summarization; store embeddings for reuse to reduce cost.

Fallbacks & runtime concerns
- If a tool times out, return partial result + warning token in the structured output.
- Retries should be idempotent; prefer per-request idempotency keys.
- Observe per-route SLOs and set dynamic timeouts (lower for user-facing, higher for async jobs).

Attachments included: tool-defs.md, schema-examples.json. We'll also include a short security checklist before the workshop (SOC2 mapping + audit log sample).

I'll send a calendar invite for Fri 9/18 10:00 AM PT and include a brief agenda.

Thanks,
Alex
